title: Defend: ECDSA hash dispatch excludes SHA-3 to prevent 32-byte collision with SHA-256
description: crypto2dev_ecdsa_hash_algo_name() (line 1346) maps digest length to hash algorithm name (32→sha256, 48→sha384, 64→sha512) but explicitly excludes SHA-3. A reviewer might add SHA3-256/SHA3-384 cases to enable ECDSA with SHA-3 digests. SHA3-256 produces 32 bytes — the same as SHA-256. Adding a SHA3-256 case would require an OR condition on the 32-byte case, but since only the digest length is known at dispatch time (the calling convention provides a pre-hashed digest, not the hash algorithm), the 32-byte entry cannot distinguish SHA-256 from SHA3-256. Silently dispatching SHA3-256 digests to the SHA-256 ECDSA path uses the wrong hash algorithm in the signature scheme, which may produce a verifiable signature under an unintended algorithm. To support ECDSA with SHA-3, the hash algorithm must be communicated via the SETKEY path (stored in key->devCtx) rather than inferred from digest length. The comment at line 1333 explains this; do not add SHA-3 cases to the switch.
